claims: The International Space Station (ISS) is a modular, habitable satellite.
The ISS serves as a microgravity research laboratory.
The ISS orbits Earth roughly every 93 minutes.
The ISS orbits at a height of about 400 km (250 miles).
The ISS is a collaborative project between the US, Russia, Europe, Japan, and Canada.
The ISS functions as a multinational, continuously occupied outpost for scientific research.
As of early 2026, the ISS is in its 74th Expedition.
The ISS is typically staffed by rotating crews on six-month missions.
The ISS hosts short-term private astronaut visits.
The ISS is 109 m long.
The ISS has an internal volume similar to a Boeing 747.
The ISS travels at roughly 27,600 km/h (17,200 mph).
The ISS completes 15.5 orbits daily.
The ISS conducts research in biology, human health, and physical sciences.
Over 50 species of plants have been grown on board the ISS.
Thousands of experiments have been performed on the ISS.
The ISS was assembled in orbit over 10 years.
The assembly of the ISS involved 42 assembly flights.
The ISS is often visible to the naked eye.
The ISS appears as a bright, fast-moving, non-flashing spot in the night sky.
The ISS is expected to remain operational until at least 2030.
There are discussions regarding potential extension of the ISS until 2032.
The ISS serves as a precursor to commercial space stations.
